title: Major Incident Simulation
scenario: At 10:15 AM on a Tuesday, the school loses access to Google Workspace. Faculty cannot log in, students cannot reach Google Classroom, and the SIS authentication is failing. The outage is school-wide. Mr. Thompson declares a major incident and asks you to be the incident commander. The CIO is in a meeting and will join the bridge in 15 minutes.
impact: Instructional and operational: 1,200 students and 150 staff are blocked from core school systems. The standardized testing window opens in 3 days. Every minute counts.
objectives: Declare the major incident and stand up the incident bridge
Open the major-incident ticket and assign the incident commander
Communicate the initial status to stakeholders within 15 minutes
Coordinate the technical investigation with the network and identity teams
Provide regular status updates to faculty and the CIO
Document the timeline and lessons learned before closing the incident
tools: Major incident bridge (conference line or video)

evidence.description: Major incident declaration record with start time, scope, and incident commander
Log of status updates sent to faculty and leadership during the incident
Post-incident review with timeline, root cause, and action items

decisionPoints.prompt: You are asked to be the incident commander. What is the first action?

options.label: Start fixing the issue immediately — every minute counts and you can coordinate later
options.feedback: An incident commander coordinates — they do not also perform the technical fix. Doing both is a recipe for an uncommanded incident.

options.label: Stand up the major incident bridge, assign a scribe and a tech lead, then coordinate
options.feedback: Correct — IC coordinates. Stand up the bridge, assign roles, and run the investigation through the tech lead while you manage comms and decisions.

options.label: Wait for the CIO to join the bridge before taking any action
options.feedback: The CIO is in a meeting. The IC must act now. The CIO joins when they are available and takes over only if escalation is needed.

decisionPoints.prompt: It is 10:25 AM. The bridge is up. Faculty are flooding the help desk. What is the right status communication now?

options.label: Wait until you have the root cause before sending a status update
options.feedback: Silence during a major incident causes panic and floods the help desk. Communicate what you know now and what you are doing.

options.label: Send a brief initial status to all faculty and the CIO: 'we are aware, we are investigating, updates every 20 minutes'
options.feedback: Correct — communicate early, briefly, and on a known cadence. Promise what you can deliver: 'next update at HH:MM'.

options.label: Send a detailed root-cause analysis to all faculty
options.feedback: Speculating on root cause before the investigation is complete will mislead stakeholders and create churn. Communicate only what is confirmed.

ticket.initialDescription: School-wide Google Workspace outage. Faculty cannot log in. SIS authentication failing. Standardized testing window in 3 days. Major incident declared at 10:18 AM by Director of Technology.

nodes.title: Receive the major incident declaration
nodes.body: Acknowledge the major incident declaration. Confirm scope: Google Workspace, SIS auth, faculty and students. Note the standardized testing window pressure. Time-box the initial response.

nodes.title: Take the IC role
nodes.body: You have been asked to be the incident commander. Choose the right first action.

nodes.title: Open the major incident ticket
nodes.body: Open the major incident ticket with type=major-incident, priority P1, and impact=high. Note the bridge details, the IC, and the declared time. Save the declaration record as evidence.

nodes.title: Issue the initial status update
nodes.body: It is 10:25 AM. Choose the right status communication strategy for the next 10 minutes.

nodes.title: Coordinate the investigation
nodes.body: The tech lead reports that the identity provider is degraded and directory sync is failing. Coordinate: confirm scope, request status from the vendor, set the next update time, and prepare the rollback if it is a config change.

nodes.title: Apply the fix
nodes.body: Apply the agreed fix: roll back the recent identity provider config change. Validate with the tech lead. Save the timeline of actions in the major incident ticket.

nodes.title: Validate the resolution
nodes.body: Confirm with the tech lead that login success rate has returned to 100%. Validate with two known-good faculty accounts. Send the all-clear communication to faculty and the CIO.

nodes.title: Write the post-incident review
nodes.body: Document the timeline, root cause, decisions made, communication cadence, and lessons learned. Schedule a post-mortem with the bridge participants within 5 business days.
nodes.prompt: Write the executive summary of the post-incident review for the CIO: timeline, root cause, what went well, and the top 3 action items.

nodes.title: Debrief
nodes.body: Review the major incident response. Key lessons: the IC coordinates, not fixes; communicate early and on a known cadence; and every major incident ends with a written post-mortem and action items.

kbOpportunity: Major incident playbook: declare → IC + tech lead + scribe → bridge → status cadence (initial, every 20 min, all-clear) → fix → post-incident review with action items within 5 business days.
